Currently · Poda

What I own
at Poda.

Not a single-lane design role. Email, sign-up, creators, social, site and visuals, one voice, built to convert across every channel a customer meets Poda in.

N°01: CRM & Email

Klaviyo, end to end

Sign-up form, welcome, post-purchase, abandoned-cart and campaign sends: strategy, copy, HTML build and the performance read. Moved campaigns to plain-text storytelling emails, +29% opens per send.

N°02: Sign-up & CRO

Designed against real objections

Sign-up form converting at 6.4%, and pages rebuilt around what actually stops a sale (price, prep time, bitterness, clumping, coffee dependence), with data deciding what shipped.

N°03: Creator Partnerships

Gifted, not paid

Sourced creators, studied every feed, wrote a custom brief per creator and followed up personally with texts, videos and voice notes. 26% → 83% delivery on gifted product alone.

N°04: AI Art Direction

Thematic AI shoots

Alt bar and family lifestyle shoots directed end to end with AI: casting, wardrobe, set, light and product placement, so the tube looks like it belongs in real life.

N°05: Social & Video

Carousels that tell a story

Storytelling Instagram carousels with big, scroll-stopping type, plus short-form video edits for Reels, built to hold attention past the first slide.

N°06: Shopify & Ecommerce

Designed, built, shipped

Homepage and landing pages built directly in Liquid, HTML, CSS and JS, keeping the matcha-smear animation alive without wrecking mobile load times.

N°07: Brand & Copy

An editorial, not a wellness brand

Defined Poda's candid, flash-heavy, slightly chaotic look and rewrote site, email and captions until nothing sounded corporate or AI-flavored.

Also directing · @drinkpoda Matcha People: an ongoing series retelling real people's stories, mostly Angelenos, through AI-generated stop-motion visuals and voiceover. Scripted and directed start to finish, open-ended rather than a fixed episode count. None released yet.

About

I'm a Lahore-based creative working end to end on how a DTC brand actually reaches someone, from the creator video and the first carousel, through the sign-up form and the Shopify checkout, to the email that brings them back. A psychology background underneath all of it: three years studying why people actually behave the way they do, now spent on why they actually buy.
